request.prompt: Which humanoid robots are commercially available?

result.text:
Several general-purpose and industrial humanoid robots have transitioned out of research labs and are commercially available for purchase, enterprise deployment, or developer integration.

Top Commercially Available Humanoid Robots

Unitree G1 (Unitree Robotics)

Type / Height: Bipedal compact humanoid (~ 1.3m)
Estimated Price: From ~ $13,500 USD on the Unitree Official Shop (with higher-spec Edu/Ultimate tiers ranging up to $60,000+)
Overview: One of the most affordable and widely accessible bipedal humanoids on the market, featuring force-controlled joints and AI-driven locomotion.

UBTECH Walker S Series (UBTECH Robotics)

Type / Height: Full-scale industrial humanoid (~ 1.7m)
Estimated Price: ~ $149,000 to $210,000 USD (available via specialized distributors like Robots International)
Overview: Built specifically for smart manufacturing and automotive assembly lines (deployed with brands like NIO and BYD), featuring 41 force-feedback servo joints and LLM-based task planning.

EngineAI T800 Pro (EngineAI)

Type / Height: Full-size bipedal humanoid
Estimated Price: ~ $63,000 USD
Overview: Positioned as an accessible mid-tier commercial and research platform for general-purpose physical tasks.

AiMOGA Mornine M1 (AiMOGA)

Type / Height: Multilingual service-oriented humanoid
Estimated Price: ~ $59,950 USD
Overview: Designed primarily for public-facing commercial applications like retail, reception, and customer interaction.

UBTECH Cruzr 1S (UBTECH Robotics)

Type / Height: Wheeled commercial service humanoid
Estimated Price: ~ $12,000 to $16,000 USD
Overview: A more budget-friendly, mobile (wheeled) alternative geared toward service, navigation, and interactive communication in commercial spaces.

Clone Robotics Protoclone

Type / Height: Bionic/anatomical musculoskeletal humanoid
Overview: A European-built bio-inspired platform featuring fluid-actuated "muscles" and an artificial skeletal structure intended for high-dexterity research and specialized deployments.

Not Yet Mass-Market Consumer Available

Boston Dynamics Atlas (All-Electric): Deployed in pilot/industrial partnership settings (such as Hyundai plants), though not sold off-the-shelf as an open consumer product.

Tesla Optimus / Figure (Figure 01 & 02): Active in factory testing or pilot commercial trials, scaling toward commercial rollout rather than broad public/retail availability yet.

Are you looking at these for industrial automation/factory work, software/AI research and development, or a commercial service/public-facing role? Let me know and I can narrow down the best fit.
